car_size_note: px_per_unit is fitted to the PixelLab art so the car is drawn about 3 units long on average over the 16 T-101 directions (Drifting, Decisions); the drawing only, the physics body is a 1 by 1 unit square. To scale the sprite to the world: scale = world size of 1 unit / px_per_unit
center_note: point in frame pixel coordinates (top-left of the frame = 0, 0) where the car's centre sits: the centre of the approved frame 4's bounding box; every other frame was moved by whole pixels to put its own bounding-box centre there
frame0_faces: world heading 0 degrees, nose along world +x: drawn pointing down-right on screen (PixelLab south-east)
frame_from_rotation: posmod(roundi(rotation / deg_to_rad(11.25)), 32) for a car body whose nose is +x at rotation 0; the same formula as the placeholder sheets
order: clockwise on screen: frame i shows world heading i * 11.25 degrees, Godot axes (y down), the same direction Godot's rotation grows
projection: PixelLab's isometric view (high top-down), drawn by PixelLab; the game draws the world in 2:1 isometric, screen = (x - y, (x + y) / 2). PixelLab's diagonals are flatter than 2:1, so the nose's angle on screen is close to, not exactly, nose_screen_angle_deg (see seen_nose_screen_angle_deg_approx per frame)
rows_note: row 0 = tilt step 1, row 1 = step 2, row 2 = step 3 (the held pose); column = the car's direction frame, as in car_iso.png (T-551's hook, car_sprite.gd tilt_frame_index)
tilt: the car's front left wheel down and its back right wheel up, about the diagonal through its front right and back left wheels; it keeps facing the same way (Drifting, Decisions, "The grind overhaul")
